text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYBEAN AND CORN SALE - Taiwan's Hui Shung Group bought a combined shipment of 38,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn from Kanematsu at a tender on Tuesday, Taipei traders said.
WHEAT SALE - Slovenia bought 40,000 tonnes U.S. hard red spring wheat for arrival by November 20, U.S. exporters said. The wheat was purchased at about $182.50 a tonne.

WHEAT SALE - Philippine flour mills have bought 41,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for immediate delivery over the weekend, traders said. Cargill sold 8,000 tonnes each of dark northern spring wheat with a 13.5 percent protein content and western white wheat. The rest was sold by a Japanese commodity house, one Manila trader said.

WHEAT TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission invited tenders for a combined cargo of 12,000 tonnes of U.S. or Canadian spring wheat and 6,000 tonnes of U.S. or Canadian durum wheat. The tender closes October 15 and shipment is November 15-30.

CORN SALE - Malaysia's Federal Flour Mills Bhd has bought 25,000 tonnes of U.S. corn for November shipment and December arrival, traders said. The consignment was priced at around $160 a tonne C&F. Another buyer was negotiating on 50,000 tonnes of corn for November shipment to trade in Malaysia, dealers said.
CORN TENDER - The Philippines will import 150,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn for December delivery, officials of the state National Food Authority said on Tuesday.

WHEAT TENDER - Algeria has launched a tender for the import of 100,000 tonnes of U.S. and/or Canadian durum wheat for shipment in December, European grain traders said. The results of the tender launched on October 7 are expected later this week. Algeria is seeking 50,000 tonnes of durum wheat for shipment in the first half of December and another 50,000 tonnes for shipment in the second half of December.

- The CCC said it is retendering for up to 35,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better hard red winter, soft white or soft red winter wheat for donation to Eritrea. Shipment was slated for Oct 30-Nov 25. Offers must be due by October 15.

WHEAT TENDERS cont'd - The Taiwan Flour Mills Association will tender on Friday for two shipments totalling 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, traders said. The shipments contain Dark Northern Spring (DNS), Hard Red Winter (HRW) and White Wheat (WW) and are slated for delivery from the Pacific Northwest.
- Sri Lanka on October 18 seeks 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat. It seeks 50,000 tonnes would be soft white wheat and 50,000 tonnes hard red winter wheat for November 11-20 shipment.

WHEAT TENDER cont'd - Armenia will be seeking 21,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for shipment up to November 20, its U.S. export agent said. The wheat would come from the European Community, Ukraine or, if U.S. origin, only hard red winter no.2. The date for offers was October 14, Yerevan, Armenia.

WHEAT AND BARLEY TENDER - The Japanese Food Agency will tender Tuesday night for a total of 80,000 tonnes U.S. wheat, 40,000 tonnes Canadian wheat and 17,000 tonnes Australian prime hard wheat, U.S.-based Japanese export firms said.
Japan will also seek 3,000 tonnes Canadian western six-row barley, 17,000 tonnes Canadian feed barley and 20,000 tonnes Australian feed barley. Shipment was due for Dec 1-Jan 10.
MARKET TALK - EC and U.S. agriculture officials were due to meet on Tuesday evening to discuss EU policy on wheat export subsidies and imports of gene-altered soybeans and corn.

... China emerged from the cocoon of last week's National Day celebrations to swoop down on the world's soybean and soymeal markets, snapping up a total of between 600,000 and 800,000 tonnes, Hong Kong traders said ... U.S. exporters believe China will continue to seek soymeal and soybeans this week. "I heard they were buying a bunch of meal," one trader said. "I think they are in for 150,000 tonnes soybean meal for October shipment. It's low pro which would be 44 percent meal."
